kind: Unregistered diagnostic; this is not evidence for a release gate
question: Why did the bounded GET-only Google adapter-versus-mount validator find no comparable file in the second active My Drive connection?
privacy: The run emitted only aggregate counts and byte totals. Account labels, identities, item IDs, paths, names, hashes, tokens and provider bodies were not recorded.

initial_result.classification: The connection had no eligible ordinary file at or below the fixed one-MiB validator limit. This was a harness boundary, not a provider or mount failure.

change_under_test.description: Keep the one-MiB default but accept an explicit per-file limit from 1 byte through 64 MiB.
change_under_test.invalid_limit_check: 67108865 bytes was refused before a live read.

interpretation: For these two exact ordinary files, the direct Google adapter bytes and mounted bytes matched. The diagnostic does not establish arbitrary-file reliability, provider-wide correctness or a release gate because its question and prediction were not registered before the run.
